claims.title: HTML pass-through branch allows unsanitized HTML/script injection
claims.text: 🟠 **P1** **HTML pass-through branch allows unsanitized HTML/script injection** When input contains any HTML-like tag, the entire string is returned completely unchanged/unescaped (`if (HTML_TAG_RE.test(text)) return text`). This means user-supplied text like `` or arbitrary script/style tags bypasses all escaping and is sent as-is to eBay, since HTML_TAG_RE only requires a single opening tag anywhere in the string to trigger full pass-through. This defeats the stated goal of this PR (XSS protection) for any description containing a tag-like substring.

claims.title: Query error from user_settings fetch is ignored
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Query error from user_settings fetch is ignored**

The result of this query destructures only `data`, discarding any `error`. If the query fails (e.g. transient DB error), `rows` will be undefined/null, `userIds` becomes an empty array, and the function completes 'successfully' having backfilled zero users. This makes failures indistinguishable from a legitimately empty result set, and Inngest will not retry.

claims.title: Per-listing and per-user failures are only logged, never surfacing as a failed step
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Per-listing and per-user failures are only logged, never surfacing as a failed step**

Failures updating individual listings are caught, logged, and counted in `failed`, but the count is never checked afterward — the step function returns normally even when every listing for a user failed to update. Similarly, the outer per-user catch block only logs and continues. This means the Inngest function will always report success regardless of how many listings actually failed to be backfilled, and there is no retry or durable record of which listings still need fixing.

claims.title: Query error is not checked before using rows
claims.text:
🟠 **P1**

**Query error is not checked before using rows**

If this query fails, `rows` will be undefined/null and `userIds` silently becomes empty, causing the backfill to report success while doing nothing. Capture and throw the error.

claims.title: Both the `user_settings` query and the `listings` query rely on Supabase's default result limit (commonly 1000 rows) with no `.range()`/pagination. On an installation with more users or listings than that limit, rows beyond the limit are silently omitted from the backfill with no warning, and the job reports success.
claims.text:
Both the `user_settings` query and the `listings` query rely on Supabase's default result limit (commonly 1000 rows) with no `.range()`/pagination. On an installation with more users or listings than that limit, rows beyond the limit are silently omitted from the backfill with no warning, and the job reports success.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
      const { data: rows, error } = await supabase
        .from('user_settings')
        .select('user_id')
        .eq('setting_key', 'ebay_refresh_token')
        .not('setting_value', 'is', null)
      if (error) throw error
      const userIds = (rows ?? []).map((r) => r.user_id as string)
```
